---
title: "Quiz · The outer delivery loop"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you
can self-grade after answering.

## 1. What are the four stages of the outer delivery loop, in order?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
1. **Review / PR** — the branch becomes a pull request that
   automated verification and human review both operate on.
2. **Merge** — the merged branch becomes the environment's source
   of truth.
3. **GitOps delivery** — a reconciler applies the merged XR to the
   target cluster.
4. **Downstream Crossplane reconciliation** — Crossplane composes
   the XR into concrete Kubernetes resources.
:::

## 2. What is the single artifact that crosses the boundary from the Sandcastle into the outer loop?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The **durable Git branch** produced by the Sandcastle (and read by
the previous lesson's hand-off). Everything the outer loop does is
derived from that branch or supplied by the environment
repository. If any outer-loop stage needs to reach back into the
Sandcastle, the hand-off did not capture enough on the branch.
:::

## 3. Why do the outer loop's guardrails belong outside the Sandcastle boundary?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Because the Sandcastle is bounded and disposable *by design*.
Putting automated verification, review, or policy inside the
Sandcastle would couple construction to delivery and delivery
policy to construction — losing the separation that makes the
Sandcastle safe to dispose of and the outer loop safe to change
independently.
:::

## 4. Which stage of the outer loop is the first one that actually touches a cluster?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Stage 3 — GitOps delivery.** Stages 1 (review / PR) and 2
(merge) are entirely repo-shaped. The cluster only appears when
the reconciler applies the merged XR, and Crossplane's own
reconciliation loop (stage 4) then composes it into concrete
Kubernetes resources.
:::

## 5. What honest prerequisites does the runnable outer-loop lab pull in that the hand-off lab did not?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
- A **learner-controlled GitHub environment repository** and an
  authenticated `gh` CLI — because stages 1–2 create a real branch,
  a real pull request, and a real merge commit that only make sense
  on a real hosted repo.
- For stages 3–4, a **Crossplane cluster** (from the
  [Hello Pico on Kubernetes lab](../../../../labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/))
  and either the `flux` CLI or `kubectl` — because those stages
  reconcile the merged XR onto a real cluster.

The lab keeps stages 1–2 runnable without a cluster (a `verify.sh
--skip-cluster` mode exits cleanly with GitHub-only assertions) so
learners can practise the review/merge half of the loop before
setting up the reconciler half.
:::
